speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy with feeding difficulties and abdominal distension; can you tell me if you have been vomiting, and if so, is the vomit green or yellow? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Since the ultrasound is normal, I need to know if there is any blood in your stool, as this could suggest a blockage like a malrotation. Also, have you noticed any signs of bilious (green) vomiting recently?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: I will check for signs of intussusception or other obstructions; can you tell me if you have noticed episodes where the baby draws their knees up to their chest or has "currant jelly" stools? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray; REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray suggests a bowel obstruction, and given the age and bilious vomiting history, I need to rule out midgut volvulus. Have you noticed if the baby has passed any stool or gas since the onset of these symptoms, and are the episodes of pain intermittent or constant? DIAGNOSIS READY: Midgut Volvulus
